title: Textbook normal
subtitle: Child · Kermany
story: This child’s radiograph is part of the model’s training set. A near-zero score here shows memory, not skill. Compare it with the adult normals in this sheet.
label: Normal

title: Textbook pneumonia
subtitle: Child · Kermany
story: Labelled pneumonia, seen in training, scored with saturated confidence. The heatmap sits on the anatomy, so this is the explanation everyone hopes for. Now look at the next case.
label: Pneumonia

title: Right answer, wrong place?
subtitle: Child · Kermany
story: Correct label, but most Grad-CAM mass falls on the image frame and padding rather than the lungs. A right answer from the wrong evidence is how shortcut learning hides inside high accuracy.
label: Pneumonia

title: Healthy adult, flagged
subtitle: Adult · Montgomery
story: An adult radiograph read as normal by radiologists, scored as pneumonia with near-certainty. The teal outline is the radiologist’s lung mask. Note where the heat peaks: on the burned-in “PA ERECT” marker, not the lungs. In step 04, the tighter crop that removes the marker turns the verdict to NORMAL. This is shortcut learning caught in the act.
licence: NLM public release, Jaeger et al. 2014
label: Normal

title: Healthy adult, cleared
subtitle: Adult · Montgomery
story: A normal adult the model gets right. Use the stress test below to see how easily that verdict flips.
licence: NLM public release, Jaeger et al. 2014
label: Normal

title: Tuberculosis, called pneumonia
subtitle: Adult · Montgomery
story: Tuberculosis is a disease this model was never taught. It can only answer NORMAL or PNEUMONIA, so abnormal lungs of any cause get pushed into one of two boxes.
licence: NLM public release, Jaeger et al. 2014
label: Tuberculosis

title: Tuberculosis, called normal
subtitle: Adult · Shenzhen
story: The same disease from another hospital, now scored normal with confidence. A binary classifier has no way to say “something else is wrong”.
licence: NLM public release, Jaeger et al. 2014
label: Tuberculosis

title: Not an X-ray
subtitle: Synthetic pattern
story: Rings and rectangles, no anatomy at all. The model still answers PNEUMONIA (0.9611). A classifier has no “I don’t know” output. Recognising an unsuitable input is the job of the system around it.
label: n/a
